newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's YUKOS share issue raises 499 bln roubles.
newsitem.headline: Russia's YUKOS share issue raises 499 bln roubles.

text.p: Oil group NK YUKOS raised 499.04 billion roubles ($91.2 million) from its sale of 579.96 million shares last month, the company said on Tuesday.
All the shares on offer were sold, and existing shareholders took up 53.38 percent of the rights issue, or 309.57 million shares, it said in a statement.
The shares, with a face value of four roubles, but priced at 909 roubles, raised authorised capital to 8.95 billion from 6.63 billion roubles, or by around 26 percent.

Following the share issue, Moscow-registered company ZAO Russkiye Investory holds 13 percent of YUKOS, YUKOS's chief spokesman Alexei Gorshkov told Reuters. He said he did not know who was behind Russkiye Investory.

But industry sources speculated that Russkiye Investory was a front company for Bank Menatep, which last year won 33 percent of YUKOS in an investment tender, and manages another 45 percent in trust under the government's shares-for-loans programme.
The issue was the first of three intended to raise about $100 million each to pay off part of its wage and tax arrears.
YUKOS owes 351.3 billion roubles in back wages and around four trillion roubles in taxes.
YUKOS is one of about a dozen vertically-integrated Russian oil companies created over the last few years.
Its main operating unit is Yuganskneftegaz YFGA.RTS 0#YFGA.RUO, Russia's second biggest oil production company, in which it holds 51 percent. ($ = 5469 Russian Roubles)
